title: Preserving a halted computation
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $S,H$ be types, and let $tm$ and $host$ be Boolean-alphabet machines with respectively $k$ and $k+1$ work tapes. Let $emb:S\to H$ and $ret:\mathrm{Bool}\to H$. Suppose that, for every state $q$, Boolean flag $over$, input symbol option $inp$, and tuple of work-tape symbols $work$, the transition of $host$ from state $emb(q,over)$ agrees with the lifted action formed from the transition of $tm$ on blank input and the last $k$ work tapes. For Boolean words $w,s$, configurations $c,d$ of $tm$ on empty input, and a natural number $T$, if $d$ is halted and $tm$ reaches $d$ from $c$ in $T$ steps, then there is a time $t\le T$ at which $host$, started from the counter configuration associated with $c$, reaches the counter configuration associated with $d$.
hypotheses_covered: tm has k work tapes and state type S
host has k+1 work tapes and state type H
the stated transition-agreement condition holds for all q, over, inp, and work
w and s are Boolean words
c and d are configurations of tm over Bool on empty input
